claims.text: Simpson's Index of Diversity is D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², where n is the number of individuals of one species, N is the total number of individuals of all species in the sample, and Σ is the sum over all species; D has no unit.

evidence.locator: Syllabus 1.2 and Annexe C (formula supplied in the examination); formulas_as_printed note in syllabus-facts.

claims.text: In mark-release-recapture a first sample of M animals is marked and released, a second sample of N animals is caught, R of them marked, and the Lincoln index estimates the population as (M × N) ÷ R; the estimate holds when marked animals mix at random, there is little migration, birth or death between samples, and marking does not change the chance of capture. The formula is not supplied in Annexe C, so it is taught here.

evidence.locator: Syllabus 1.2 (mark-release-recapture using the Lincoln index); source note in syllabus-facts that Annexe C contains no Lincoln index.
